column1: # reason-kind-adjudications.tsv -- the HAND layer under scripts/classify_writeoff_reasons.py
# WHAT THIS IS. The classifier derives a kind from the words in a reason cell. Where the
# unit of reasoning is NOT the cell -- because the cell is a pointer at a ruling that 61
# rows share -- deriving a kind from keywords over a 950-to-2735-character argument is not
# a measurement, it is a word count. Those rulings are adjudicated ONCE, here, by hand.
# FOUR FIELDS, TAB SEPARATED:
#   1  key     `RULING R<n>` for a network.md ruling section, or a slice-qualified row id
#              (`J 134`, `P B10`). NEVER a line number: `the-contingent-writeoffs.md` s4.1
#              measured all six of the census's line-number locators drifting 48 to 51
#              lines, one of them landing on a DIFFERENT row that read COVERED-PROVEN.
#   2  kind    one or more of US-RULING, US-BOUNDARY, WORLD-FACT, ACCOUNT-FACT,
#              PROCESS-FACT, joined by `+`. UNCLEAR is legal and means the honest answer
#              is that nobody can tell from what is written.
#   3  quote   A VERBATIM SUBSTRING of the thing being ruled on, which must still be
#              present or `--check` FAILS. This is the entire anti-staleness mechanism:
#              when somebody rewrites a reason out from under a hand judgement, the
#              judgement goes RED instead of silently mislabelling the row. Single-line
#              only -- the census wraps its quoted source at ~76 columns, so a phrase that
#              spans a line break will never match.
#   4  why     one line, for a reader who wants to disagree with me.
# A `#` line is a comment. Blank lines are ignored.
key

column3: the ruling is that nobody should
column4: /mynetwork/ is refused because loading it resets a pending-invitation badge and the cost lands on the people whose invitations get marked seen. A decision, defended, and it states its own circularity: the measurement that would overturn it requires spending the thing it protects. Durable.

column1: RULING R2
column3: catching a read that has nothing to do with inviting
column4: FOUR SUBSTRINGS SOMEBODY TYPED, checked before the allowlist. The ruling's own text admits the collateral: the connections list is unreachable only because its address contains /invite and /connect. That is a line, not a decision about connections, and nothing in the 20 rows beneath it says so.

column1: RULING R3
column3: read live on his own profile on 2026-08-30
column4: Two facts braided. The refusal rests on a MEASUREMENT taken on HIS profile -- zero endorse controls among 222 live controls -- which is an account fact that one received endorsement would falsify. The third-party half is ours (R4). The cell's own history records the reason being REPLACED from policy to measurement, which is what makes the account dependency invisible.

column1: RULING R4
column3: cost lands entirely on somebody who is not him
column4: Loading a stranger's profile spends THEIR privacy on OUR measurement. Ours, permanent, and argued from the receiving end rather than asserted. Note the ruling flags its own scope gap: the text says "may not do it for a MEASUREMENT" and 10 of its 14 rows are ACTS, not measurements.

column1: RULING R5

column4: A design decision at any confirm level, and five other specs cite it in reversible_by. Ours and durable.

column1: RULING R6

column4: We refuse to defeat viewer anonymity. The refusal is ours; the constraint it respects is LinkedIn's anonymity feature and what it renders him, which is a world fact.

column1: RULING R9
column3: That is roughly one send per week
column4: THE MOST CONTINGENT RULING IN THE SLICE and its name says none of it. Four independent grounds: LinkedIn's invitation cap is behavioural and automation-suspicion-driven (WORLD); he has 5 InMail credits a month so automating five acts a month is ceremony (ACCOUNT -- arithmetic over an allowance); he holds a paid subscription a restriction would strand (ACCOUNT); the skill recommends only and must never send (US-RULING). The arithmetic ground weakens the moment the allowance changes.

column3: read and type out your responses
column4: THE ROW IS ITS OWN REOPENER AND NOBODY NOTICED. Capability: "Practice by reading and typing responses instead". Reason: the practice interview is a real-time SPOKEN session needing camera and microphone, REOPENER "a text-only interview mode". The cell opens by quoting LinkedIn's own help text "read and type out your responses" -- so the evidence it cites documents the very mode whose absence is the write-off. Classified WORLD-FACT because what is actually in question is whether LinkedIn draws a text mode, which nothing here measured.
